rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all eight compounds and identify critical pairs while limiting the time penalty. The retention window will guide subsequent narrowing and slope or temperature tests.

Halve the gradient slope while holding the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed to test whether the clustered peaks separate with a shallower gradient. This should distinguish slope-responsive pairs from those requiring temperature selectivity changes.

The shallower gradient resolved most of the cluster, leaving one critical pair. Raise temperature to test selectivity for that pair while shortening retention and preserving the successful gradient slope.

Slightly flatten the gradient at the best temperature to try to lift the remaining R = 1.10 pair above 1.5. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, allowing a resolution gain without a time penalty.

The critical late pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so move to a steeper gradient than injection 3. This should improve that pair and shorten the run, while testing whether the earlier R = 1.61 pair retains sufficient resolution.

Injection 5 is nearly optimal, with only one pair just below baseline resolution. Lower temperature by one grid step to adjust selectivity while retaining its successful gradient slope and ample margin below 10 minutes.

Return to 60 C and raise the starting organic fraction one step to fine-tune both slope and selectivity near the best method. This tests whether the marginal early pair can reach R = 1.5 without sacrificing the late pair.

Use a narrower solvent window to obtain a slope slightly shallower than injection 7, targeting its two marginal early pairs while preserving the late pair’s resolution margin. The final organic fraction remains comfortably above the observed elution window, so all peaks should elute during the gradient.

Reduce the slope slightly from 0.04583 to 0.045 organic fraction per minute to bring the R = 1.49 pair above threshold while retaining the late pair’s margin. The endpoint remains above the last peak’s estimated elution fraction, with retention comfortably below 10 minutes.

Injection 9 already achieves the maximum CRF; now test a shorter fully resolved separation by raising the starting organic fraction. A slightly shallower slope compensates for compression of the early cluster, while injection 9 remains the proven optimum-score fallback.

Flatten the gradient at the higher starting organic fraction to recover resolution in the early cluster, using the late pair’s R = 2.06 margin. This tests whether full resolution can be restored with the last peak still earlier than injection 9.

The high-temperature refinements show opposing slope requirements for the critical pairs, so test a substantially different temperature for a new selectivity pattern. This moderately steep gradient should keep all eight compounds observable with limited risk of a time penalty; injection 9 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Steepen the low-temperature gradient to test the remaining critical pair’s slope response and shorten the separation. Monitor the late R = 1.65 pair for loss of resolution; injection 9 remains the proven maximum-score method.

Return to injection 12’s slope and raise temperature by 10 C to test whether selectivity resolves its lone critical pair while shortening retention. This explores an intermediate-temperature alternative without disturbing the proven maximum-score method from injection 9.

Test 45 C at the established slope to look for a shorter fully resolved separation after the temperature-driven elution-order changes. Injection 9 already achieves the maximum possible CRF and remains the fallback.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient at 45 C to improve the lone critical pair while limiting retention time. This explores a shorter alternative to injection 9, which already attains the maximum CRF.

Test whether a larger shift in starting organic fraction produces a favorable elution-order change and a shorter separation at 60 C. This is exploratory: injection 9 remains the proven maximum-score method, and the early peaks must be checked for compression.

At 25 C, the critical pair improved with a shallower gradient; reduce the slope to 0.04 while raising the starting organic fraction to offset longer retention. This tests another route to full resolution below 10 minutes, with injection 9 retained as the proven maximum-score method.

Slightly reduce the slope from 0.0400 to 0.0375 to lift injection 18’s lone R = 1.40 pair above threshold. The last peak is expected to remain below 10 minutes, potentially establishing a second maximum-score method at low temperature.

Raise both solvent endpoints by one step while preserving injection 19’s successful slope to shorten the low-temperature separation. Its minimum resolution of 1.73 provides some margin for selectivity changes, while injection 9 remains the faster proven maximum-score method.

Reduce the slope at injection 20’s starting composition to recover its lone unresolved pair. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially combining full resolution with a shorter run than the low-temperature method from injection 19.

Raise the starting organic fraction and flatten the gradient to compensate for the critical pair’s loss of resolution at higher starting strength. This tests a more tightly focused low-temperature method while retaining injection 9 as the fastest proven maximum-score method.

Test a further shift to a narrower, shallower low-temperature gradient, compensating for the critical pair’s sensitivity to starting organic fraction. Injection 9 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method; this run tests whether stronger initial elution can shorten the alternative separation without losing resolution.

Return near injection 9 and test a slightly shallower slope to improve its marginal early-pair resolution, while checking whether the late pair stays above 1.5. Injection 9 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the preferred method if this adjustment sacrifices resolution.

Use the final injection to test a slightly steeper gradient near the fastest maximum-score method, seeking shorter retention while checking the marginal early pairs. Injection 9 remains the recommended method unless this run also achieves full resolution.
